openings.claim: Replaying both ordering rules on one frozen record extract per pair could isolate ordering effects from subset differences.
openings.delta: Replace separate subset inputs with a shared, cited extract carrying manifest position, timestamps, boundary digests and unknowns. Retain the manifest ledger; add a timestamp-priority shadow replay using the same uncertainty rules. A local script performs comparisons; log every manual inspection across both variants, including rereads, within twelve per pair and sixty minutes. Report all six pairs with a supported stage or unresolved interval and a supplied-resource next check.
openings.prediction: Nearest rival: G0437:R1 applied separately to disjoint subsets. Shared inputs eliminate subset composition as an explanation for within-pair disagreement. The export-before-parse timestamp can distinguish priorities; different cited earliest boundaries or interval widths would distinguish outputs. Identical outputs would defeat a claim that ordering changed these conclusions. Missing transform digests or removed records must remain unknown, never evidence of nonexecution.
openings.probe: Build the extract from supplied records and dictionary; replay both variants over each three-pair subset. Apply stipulated final-review removals to both inputs, invalidate dependent claims and freeze outputs before opening answer sheets. Use twenty additional minutes to compare within-pair disagreements, answer-sheet support and inspection counts. A next check inspects an available adjacent record if allowance remains, or checks digest comparability against the dictionary; otherwise retain unresolved status.
assumptions: Script implementation and extract verification must fit available time; this capacity is unproved. Incomplete replay cannot establish comparative advantage.
Manifest stages identify expected order, not observed execution chronology. Equal digests do not exclude transient earlier divergence.
Defeat: boundary alignment is unsupported, removals destroy distinguishing evidence, or no discordant outputs occur. Explain mismatches separately; blank warnings prove nothing.

attacks.dependency: Separate subset results support a comparison despite differing cases.

assessment: A proposed comparative probe, not deployment or demonstrated improvement. Shared inputs remove one confound but do not guarantee an informative result.

lineage.reason: Preserve the cited boundary ledger; replace disjoint-input comparison with shared-input replay.
